### Making a Fun Cat Map

First thing's first, let's load the libraries:


```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(maps)
library(mapdata)
library(mapproj)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(ggthemes)
```


---


### Import Cats Data from UK Cats

Let's bring in the data:

```{r}

cats_uk <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2023/2023-01-31/cats_uk.csv')

cats_uk_reference <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2023/2023-01-31/cats_uk_reference.csv')


```

### Add the UK mapdata

First, take the world data

```{r}

world <- map_data("world")

head(world)

```

Then, extract the region

```{r}

#Combine the data to get the british isles:
BI_data <- world |> 
  filter(region == "Ireland"| region == "UK")

```

Time to make a base map of the British Isles!

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
# Map of UK+Ireland island area

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = BI_data,
               color = "black",
               fill = "lightgray",
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "#E7F6FF",
                     color = "#E7F6ff"),
        panel.grid.major = 
          element_line(color = "#D3E6ff"),
        axis.line =
          element_line(color = "#D3E6ff"),
        title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Map of the British Isles",
       x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude")+
  guides(fill = "none")

```

Ok! Adding some points maybe?

```{r}

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = BI_data,
               color = "black",
               fill = "lightgray",
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator")+
  geom_point(data = cats_uk,
             aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat,
                 group = tag_id))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "#E7F6FF",
                     color = "#E7F6ff"),
        panel.grid.major = 
          element_line(color = "#D3E6ff"),
        axis.line =
          element_line(color = "#D3E6ff"),
        title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Map of the British Isles",
       x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude")+
  guides(fill = "none")


```

Wow, they're alllllll at the bottom. Let's see if we can zoom in.

```{r}

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = BI_data,
               color = "black",
               fill = "lightgray",
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group))+
  coord_map(projection = "mercator",
            xlim = c(-7,-3),
            ylim = c(50, 52))+
  geom_point(data = cats_uk,
             aes(x = location_long, y = location_lat,
                 group = tag_id))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(panel.background =
          element_rect(fill = "#E7F6FF",
                     color = "#E7F6ff"),
        panel.grid.major = 
          element_line(color = "#D3E6ff"),
        axis.line =
          element_line(color = "#D3E6ff"),
        title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Map of the British Isles",
       x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude")+
```

Wow that looks Terrible. I'm not sure how to make the resolution less.... awful?


OK let's try something different. Let's start with an sf map:

```{r}
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)

world_sf <- ne_countries(scale = "medium",
                         returnclass = "sf")

ggplot(world_sf) +
  geom_sf(fill = "lightgray",
          color = "white") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-7,-3),
          ylim = c(50, 52))+
  theme_classic()
```

### Plastic Pollution!

First, load in the data 

```{r}

plastics <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2021/2021-01-26/plastics.csv')

```

Let's see what this data looks like:

```{r}

head(plastics, n = 4)

```

OK-- this looks like something I can work with! 

So, going back to the base map data:

```{r}

world <- map_data("world")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, 
                   y = lat,
                   group = group,
                   fill = region),
               color = "black")+
  guides(fill = "none")

```

OK so that's a good base map to start with. Let's look at the plastics data again. We could do a number of events per country heatmap. We could also do a number of participants, or amount of plastic per country. We could do all three.

Let's first try to make a number of events per country.

First we must full_join the two datasets. Where do they match up? region/country. The headings are different. Let's fix that.

```{r}

plastics |> 
  rename(region = country) |> 
  #then, inner_join
  full_join(world) -> world_plastics

```

OK that dataset seems a bit massive. Let's see how it looks.

```{r}
head(world_plastics)
```

OK, that's a bit too massive. Plotting it didn't really work. Let's see if we can slim it down somehow.

What if we only looked at Coke plastics?

```{r}

world_plastics |> 
  filter(parent_company == "The Coca-Cola Company") -> coke_plastics


coke_plastics |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, y = lat,
                   group = group),
               fill = "lightgray")+
  geom_polygon(aes(x = long, 
                   y = lat,
                   group = group,
                   fill = grand_total))+
  scale_fill_continuous(palette = c("yellow", "orange", "red"))

```

Ok let's try with more than just coke plastics.

```{r}

world_plastics |> 
  filter(parent_company == "The Coca-Cola Company"| 
         parent_company == "PepsiCo"|
         parent_company == "Nestlé") |> 
  filter_out(grand_total == "0") -> us_plastics


us_plastics |> 
  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = world,
                 aes(x = long, y = lat,
                     group = group),
                 fill = "gray")+
    geom_polygon(aes(x = long, 
                     y = lat,
                     group = group,
                     fill = log(grand_total)))+
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = c("yellow", "orange", "red"),
                         guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal",
                                                 title.position = "bottom"))+
    facet_wrap(~parent_company, ncol=2)+
    theme_grey()+
    theme(legend.position = c(0.8,0.2),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
          plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
          plot.tag.position = c(0.81,0.35))+
    labs(fill = NULL,
         title = "Amount of Nestlé, Pepsi, and Coke Plastics Collected per Country",
         subtitle = "Collected during Break Free From Plastic Cleanup Events",
         caption = "Gray = no data available",
         x = "Longitude",
         y = "Latitude",
         tag = "Log of Total Plastic")

```
